test_title: RRB NTPC CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 30 Jan 2021 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Which system has been adopted by the Reserve Bank of India for note issue?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Minimum Reserve System.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

 
• The **Minimum Reserve System** is the currency issue system followed by the RBI to issue currency notes at present.
 
• It was adopted in 1956. The Proportional Reserve system was used to issue notes before 1956.
 
• The Minimum Reserve System requires the RBI to keep a minimum reserve of **Rs 200 crores** comprising foreign currencies, gold coins, and gold bullion. 
 
• Out of this** 200 crore, a minimum of 115 crores rupee** should be in the form of Gold or gold bullion, and the rest should be in the form of foreign currencies.
 
• There is no limit for the RBI to issue currencies by keeping this minimum reserve.
